socfpga_i2c.h

I2C hardware abstraction driver interface for the SoCFPGA bare-metal software stack.

Constants
SOCFPGA_I2C_RESET_NONE

A sentinel value passed to the configuration structure to indicate that the driver should bypass interacting with the Reset Manager during initialization.

Types
socfpga_i2c_handle_t

An opaque software handle representing an active connection to an I2C Master hardware instance. It encapsulates the MMIO base address, active buffer pointers, transaction state machines, and remaining byte counts.

socfpga_i2c_callback_t

Function signature invoked by the I2C Interrupt Service Routine (ISR) when an asynchronous background transfer completes or encounters a fatal bus fault (e.g., Target NACK or Arbitration Lost).

Parameters
handle

The active I2C instance handle.

status

Hardware completion status (0 for success, negative for bus faults).

context

Opaque user pointer passed back to the caller.

socfpga_i2c_config_t

Defines the initial hardware state and timing parameters for the I2C controller.

socfpga_i2c_info_t

Reports what the driver established about a controller during initialization.

socfpga_i2c_init
int32_t socfpga_i2c_init(
const 
socfpga_i2c_config_t 
*
config,
socfpga_i2c_handle_t 
*
handle
)

Initializes the I2C Master controller. This un-gates the peripheral clock, cycles the hardware reset line via the Reset Manager, and configures the IC_CON (Control) and IC_TAR (Target Address) registers based on the provided parameters.

Parameters
config
const socfpga_i2c_config_t*

Pointer to the hardware configuration parameters.

handle
socfpga_i2c_handle_t*

Pointer to store the resulting opaque active instance handle.

Returns

0 on success; -EBUSY if no descriptor is free or the instance is already open; -EINVAL for bad config; -ENODEV when no controller answers at base_address; -ERANGE when the input clock cannot produce the requested bus frequency.

int32_t socfpga_i2c_get_info(
socfpga_i2c_handle_t 
handle,
socfpga_i2c_info_t 
*
info
)

Reports the controller identity, input clock, programmed SCL counts and FIFO depths established at initialization. Useful for bring-up, where the question is usually whether the controller is reachable and clocked at all.

Parameters
handle
socfpga_i2c_handle_t

The active I2C instance handle.

info
socfpga_i2c_info_t*

Output storage for the controller description.

Returns

0 on success; -EINVAL for a NULL handle or output pointer.

socfpga_i2c_set_target_address
int32_t socfpga_i2c_set_target_address(
socfpga_i2c_handle_t 
handle,
uint16_t 
target_address
)

Retargets an open handle at a different device address without tearing down and re-initializing the controller.

Parameters
handle
socfpga_i2c_handle_t

The active I2C instance handle.

target_address
uint16_t

The 7-bit or 10-bit address to address next.

Returns

0 on success; -EINVAL for a bad handle or address; -EBUSY during a transfer.

socfpga_i2c_probe
int32_t socfpga_i2c_probe(
socfpga_i2c_handle_t 
handle,
uint16_t 
target_address
)

Addresses a device and reports whether it acknowledges, without interpreting any data it returns. This is the primitive a bus scan is built from.

The handle is left targeting target_address, so a scan does not have to restore the previous target between probes.

Parameters
handle
socfpga_i2c_handle_t

The active I2C instance handle.

target_address
uint16_t

The 7-bit or 10-bit address to test.

Returns

0 when the device acknowledges; -ENXIO when it does not; -ETIMEDOUT when the bus itself does not respond.

socfpga_i2c_recover_bus
int32_t socfpga_i2c_recover_bus(
socfpga_i2c_handle_t 
handle
)

Cancels any in-flight transfer, flushes both FIFOs and returns the master to idle after a transfer left the bus wedged.

Parameters
handle
socfpga_i2c_handle_t

The active I2C instance handle.

Returns

0 when the bus returns to idle; -ETIMEDOUT when it stays busy.

socfpga_i2c_get_abort_source
int32_t socfpga_i2c_get_abort_source(
socfpga_i2c_handle_t 
handle,
uint32_t 
*
source
)

Returns the IC_TX_ABRT_SOURCE value captured from the most recent failed transfer, so a caller can distinguish an address NACK from a data NACK, lost arbitration, or a protocol error.

The value is latched by the transfer itself because reading IC_CLR_TX_ABRT to release the TX FIFO also clears the source register.

Parameters
handle
socfpga_i2c_handle_t

The active I2C instance handle.

source
uint32_t*

Output storage for the abort source bitmap.

Returns

0 on success; -EINVAL for a NULL handle or output pointer.

Constants
SOCFPGA_I2C_ABORT_ADDR_NACK

Mirrors the IC_TX_ABRT_SOURCE bit that reports a 7-bit address going unacknowledged, so an application can test for an absent device without including the register header.

socfpga_i2c_abort_source_str
const char *socfpga_i2c_abort_source_str(
uint32_t 
source
)

Names the dominant cause in an IC_TX_ABRT_SOURCE value so a log line is readable without a register reference. The flushed-byte count in the upper bits is ignored.

Parameters
source
uint32_t

A value obtained from socfpga_i2c_get_abort_source.

Returns

A static string describing the cause, never NULL.

socfpga_i2c_abort_flush_count
uint32_t socfpga_i2c_abort_flush_count(
uint32_t 
source
)

Extracts the number of bytes the abort discarded from the TX FIFO, which tells a caller how much of its payload never reached the bus.

Parameters
source
uint32_t

A value obtained from socfpga_i2c_get_abort_source.

Returns

The flushed byte count.

socfpga_i2c_deinit
int32_t socfpga_i2c_deinit(
socfpga_i2c_handle_t 
handle
)

Safely halts the I2C Master controller. This masks all interrupts, disables the IP block (aborting any ongoing bus transactions), and frees the software descriptor memory.

Parameters
handle
socfpga_i2c_handle_t

The active I2C instance handle to shut down.

Returns

0 on success.

socfpga_i2c_close
int32_t socfpga_i2c_close(
socfpga_i2c_handle_t 
handle
)

Halts the I2C software context without asserting the physical hardware reset line or destroying the active bus configuration.

Parameters
handle
socfpga_i2c_handle_t

The active I2C instance handle.

Returns

0 on success.

socfpga_i2c_write_sync
int32_t socfpga_i2c_write_sync(
socfpga_i2c_handle_t 
handle,
const 
uint8_t 
*
buffer,
size_t 
length
)

Executes a blocking write transaction. The driver formats the data and pushes it into the Transmit (TX) FIFO by writing to the IC_DATA_CMD register. It spin-polls the IC_STATUS register until the TX FIFO is empty and the bus returns to an idle state.

Parameters
handle
socfpga_i2c_handle_t

The active I2C instance handle.

buffer
const uint8_t*

Pointer to the byte array payload to transmit.

length
size_t

The number of bytes to push to the bus.

Returns

0 on success; -ETIMEDOUT or -EIO if the target NACKs the address or data.

socfpga_i2c_read_sync
int32_t socfpga_i2c_read_sync(
socfpga_i2c_handle_t 
handle,
uint8_t 
*
buffer,
size_t 
length
)

Executes a blocking read transaction. The driver issues read requests to the IC_DATA_CMD register (which drives the SCL line to clock data in from the target) and spin-polls the Receive (RX) FIFO to extract the incoming bytes.

Parameters
handle
socfpga_i2c_handle_t

The active I2C instance handle.

buffer
uint8_t*

Pointer to the destination memory buffer.

length
size_t

The exact number of bytes to clock in from the target.

Returns

0 on success; -ETIMEDOUT if the target fails to supply data.

socfpga_i2c_write_then_read_sync
int32_t socfpga_i2c_write_then_read_sync(
socfpga_i2c_handle_t 
handle,
const 
uint8_t 
*
tx_buffer,
size_t 
tx_length,
uint8_t 
*
rx_buffer,
size_t 
rx_length
)

Executes a blocking, combined format transaction utilizing a repeated START condition.

This is the standard mechanism for reading from EEPROMs or I2C sensors: the master writes the internal register/memory address, issues a repeated START (preventing other masters from claiming the bus), and then immediately reads back the requested data payload.

Parameters
handle
socfpga_i2c_handle_t

The active I2C instance handle.

tx_buffer
const uint8_t*

Pointer to the data to transmit (usually the internal register address).

tx_length
size_t

Number of bytes to transmit.

rx_buffer
uint8_t*

Pointer to the destination buffer for the incoming data.

rx_length
size_t

Number of bytes to clock in from the target.

Returns

0 on success.

Initiates an interrupt-driven write transaction. The driver primes the TX FIFO and enables the TX_EMPTY interrupt mask before returning control to the caller.

handle
socfpga_i2c_handle_t

The active I2C instance handle.

buffer
const uint8_t*

Pointer to the payload. Must remain valid until the callback fires.

length
size_t

Number of bytes to transmit.

callback
socfpga_i2c_callback_t

Function to invoke upon completion or fault.

context
void*

Opaque user pointer passed back to the callback.

Returns

0 if the transfer successfully queues; -EBUSY if the controller is already active.

socfpga_i2c_isr
void socfpga_i2c_isr(
void 
*
param
)

The primary Interrupt Service Routine for the I2C controller. This function reads the IC_INTR_STAT register, manages the TX/RX FIFOs, and handles fatal errors (TX_ABRT). It invokes user callbacks when background state machines reach terminal states.

Parameters
param
void*

The opaque socfpga_i2c_handle_t context passed from the Exception vector.

socfpga_i2c_wait_async_complete
int32_t socfpga_i2c_wait_async_complete(
socfpga_i2c_handle_t 
handle,
uint32_t 
timeout
)

Drives an outstanding asynchronous transfer to completion by servicing the controller from the calling context, so the asynchronous engine can be used on a system that has not routed the I2C interrupt to the GIC.

This does not prove interrupt delivery; it exercises the same state machine the ISR runs.

Parameters
handle
socfpga_i2c_handle_t

The active I2C instance handle.

timeout
uint32_t

Maximum time in microseconds to wait, or 0 to use the handle's own.

Returns

0 once no transfer is outstanding; -ETIMEDOUT if one is still in flight. The transfer's own status is reported through its completion callback.
